Run a new realtime session core in shadow of the current one for OpenAI-protocol connections

The core keeps the conversation as entities keyed by the ids the connection reports
(responses, spoken turns, inputs, reply obligations), applies every event and caller
command in one synchronous transition, and projects history from them without
editing a recorded message. It runs only in shadow, behind a private switch the
test suite turns on: the session's own history and behavior are unchanged.

Settle what the shadow core waits on when the connection or the session gives up

- a lossy reconnect ends spoken turns whose transcript it loses, loses requests the
  connection no longer counted as active, and settles refusals carried for a
  provider-started response that never came; so does the next response and a close
- a turn xAI adds while it is still spoken ends, with its audio, at the speech end
- joined turns end when the session stops reading
- a tool call the session refuses over a usage limit is left out, and results of an
  abandoned tool batch ask for no reply
- only inputs history records are kept, and placed without rescanning the rest
- shadow comparison covers the whole usage
- accepted finding SIM-24 for the pre-echo inference; SIM-1 and SIM-15 no longer
  pending; every pinned scenario is also run to its end to judge the core

Keep OpenAI-protocol realtime history, usage, and reply waits in the session core

OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, and xAI sessions now take all_messages(), new_messages(),
usage, and wait_for_reply() from the new session core; the current one still
streams the events, runs the tools, and owns the spans. A private switch
(_session._CORE_MODE = 'legacy') brings the current behavior back.

- history follows the provider's conversation and only grows; a reply waits for
  the transcript of the spoken turn before it, up to five seconds after it's done
- phase of gpt-realtime-2.x assistant messages is kept in provider_details
- the simulator judges the core directly: fixed findings are now regression
  tests, the rest narrowed to Gemini and GPT-Live; new findings SIM-25 and SIM-26

Take realtime history, usage, and reply waits from the session core on OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, and xAI

Third step of the realtime session refactor, stacked on #9422 (the new session core, in shadow).

OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and xAI sessions now take their history, usage and reply waits from the new session core (`realtime/_core.py`) instead of the current one. The current one still turns the connection's events into the ones the session streams, runs the tools, and owns the spans. A private switch (`_session._CORE_MODE = 'legacy'`) brings back the current behavior. Gemini Live and GPT-Live are unchanged: their connections don't report identified lifecycle events yet.

> [!WARNING]
> **Compatibility impact:** On OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and xAI, `all_messages()` / `new_messages()` follow the order of the provider's own conversation, and a message appears there only once everything before it is final, so a reply can appear a little after it ends. A few spoken turns are recorded differently (below). With `audio_retention`, the conversation tools see as `RunContext.messages` and the input messages on response spans no longer carry retained audio (transcripts only); `all_messages()`, the streamed events and the span's response keep it. This lasts until the current core is removed and both read the core's history.
>
> **Why this can ship in a minor release:** each change fixes a known bug the realtime simulator found or reproduced from recordings: turns recorded out of the provider's order, history snapshots that weren't prefixes of later ones, and `wait_for_reply()` hangs and early returns.
>
> **Migration:** none needed. Code that reads `all_messages()` right after `wait_for_reply()` should expect the reply to appear once the transcript of the spoken turn before it has arrived (at most 30 seconds after the reply ends).

### What changes for users (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, xAI)

- **History follows the provider's conversation.** A spoken turn sits where the provider added it; text, images and tool results where they reached it. A turn the user started during a reply, but which the provider committed after that reply ended, is now recorded after the reply. This reverses #8764's speaking order for that one case, as decided on the refactor (SIM-11).
- **Snapshots only grow.** Nothing is inserted ahead of what `all_messages()` already returned; a tool's return still directly follows its call. Instead of inserting a late transcript (finding E), a reply waits for the transcript of the spoken turn before it. That wait is bounded: 30 seconds counted from the reply being ready, after which the turn is recorded with the transcript it has.
- **`wait_for_reply()` waits for exactly what it owes:** the replies to inputs sent so far, followed through tool rounds, settled by the response the provider says answers them, or by a refusal, a lost connection, or a parked error. It no longer returns before a started server-VAD reply (SIM-2b), or hangs after a refused tool-results request, a barge-in that drops a deferred request, a lost refusal, or a reply lost to a drop (SIM-1, SIM-3, SIM-12, SIM-15, SIM-16, SIM-20, SIM-21).
- **Usage** is counted per response id, so a repeated or late terminal no longer counts a second request (the history half of 8801), and the request limit doesn't count a server-VAD reply twice.
- **`phase`** (`commentary` / `final_answer`) of `gpt-realtime-2.x` assistant messages is kept as `'phase'` in the part's `provider_details`, as a standard OpenAI Responses run records it. It can't be sent back: the realtime API rejects `item.phase` on `conversation.item.create`.
- **xAI push-to-talk:** commits made while a reply is still under way go out together after it, so xAI makes one turn of them, and history now has one. A commit still held back when the session closes made no turn, and history now has none (the current core recorded a content-less turn for each). Both match what xAI's conversation has (decided on review); with `audio_retention='input_audio'`, the audio of a commit that never went out is no longer kept.

### Simulator

- The shadow checker is gone: the session's history *is* the core's now, so the ordinary invariants judge it.
- Fixed for OpenAI-protocol sessions and turned into `run_clean` regression tests: OR9, SIM-1 (started reply), SIM-2a, SIM-2b (VAD), SIM-3, SIM-11, SIM-12, SIM-14, SIM-15 (both scenarios), SIM-16, SIM-20, SIM-21, E, and from #9352: SIM-26, SIM-27, SIM-28, SIM-29, SIM-31, SIM-32, SIM-35.
  - Deleted: OR9, SIM-3, SIM-12, SIM-14, SIM-16, SIM-20, SIM-26, SIM-27, SIM-28, SIM-29, SIM-31, SIM-32, SIM-35.
  - Still pinned from #9352, as the core has them: SIM-25, SIM-30, SIM-34, SIM-36, 8763c #3.
  - Narrowed to the providers still on the current core: E, SIM-2a, SIM-2b, SIM-11, each with a Gemini (or GPT-Live) pinned scenario found by exploration.
  - Still pinned for the OpenAI protocol, with scenarios that reproduce on the core: SIM-1 (a lost server-VAD reply that called a tool), SIM-15 (a raising tool, on xAI), SIM-21 (xAI, which resumes the conversation).
- New findings, pinned (the two open review items from #9422):
  - SIM-37: clearing the audio while the user still speaks ends a turn xAI already added, so the transcript xAI still sends is dropped.
  - SIM-38: a `speech_stopped` that server VAD takes back (no commit follows) becomes an empty user turn the provider never had, after holding history back. Both rest on fake-server guesses (no recording has either), which is why they're pinned rather than fixed here.
- New invariants: `history.transcript_lost` (a transcript the session read isn't in history) and `history.phantom_turn` (history has a spoken turn the provider didn't).
- Exploration at 2000 examples per OpenAI-protocol dialect over many seeds finds nothing unregistered. Gemini and GPT-Live explorations still hit pre-existing, unregistered violations on main (a Gemini async-tool `wait.hang`, an OpenAI-legacy `history.order`), reproduced on `origin/main`.

### Notes

- `retain_audio_max_seconds` bounds the audio the core keeps in history the same way it bounds the session's, consistent with `retain_images_max`: the core keeps its own budget, counts the audio it records, the audio of turns waiting for their transcript and what is still coming in, and evicts the oldest first, each part keeping its transcript.
- Recorded audio is held once: the session's own record (what feeds `RunContext.messages` and span inputs) lets go of retained audio once the core keeps history. Audio of a turn still being spoken or a response still coming in is buffered twice until the turn or response ends, each copy bounded by `retain_audio_max_seconds` (the current core's input buffer is trimmed after each send that succeeds, so while a send is stalled and more `send_audio()` calls queue up behind it, that copy can briefly run over, as it already could): the current core builds the streamed `PartEndEvent` parts (and span outputs) from its own buffers, and the core needs its own for history. That goes away with the current core.
- A conversation id the session resolves late (`RealtimeSession.conversation`) reaches the messages the core recorded before it, as it does the session's.

- A reconnect that replays local history (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI) replays the provider's conversation as far as it went, including what `all_messages()` still holds back: a spoken turn waiting for its transcript (with what it has) and the messages after it, and, last, inputs sent that the provider hadn't acknowledged before the drop (#9352's `history.not_restored` invariant caught those missing).
- `send_audio()` hands each chunk to the core under the send lock, so overlapping sends reach it in the order they go out, and a failed send takes back its own chunk, not one still waiting.
- A tool call repeated for a response still open, or part of a resumed xAI conversation's replay, is recorded once, as the session runs it once.
- A tool's return still goes directly after its call, even when later messages were already returned: the one exception to snapshots only growing, as before, now stated in the docs.

- `RunContext.messages` and the chat spans' input messages keep using the history the current core builds as it streams, which has a response by its tool calls.
- The event stream still comes from the current core, so `phase` is only in history, not on `PartStartEvent`.

- Part of the realtime session refactor (no issue).

**Medium: Evicted image payloads remain in memory**

With the core now enabled by default, a client whose image frames are forwarded through `send(..., respond=False)` can exhaust host memory despite `retain_images_max`: `SessionCore._withdraw()` only sets `withdrawn`, leaving the request and its image bytes strongly referenced by `_inputs` and `_placed` or `_unplaced`. Release the withdrawn request payload from these collections rather than only hiding it from `all_messages()`.
